title: Daily Market Digest: July 28, 2026
subtitle: Market sentiment mixed as investors eye Big Tech earnings and Fed decision.

items.headline: Futures Mixed Ahead of Tech Earnings and Fed Meeting
items.summary: U.S. stock futures traded mixed on Tuesday as investors awaited a crucial week featuring a wave of Big Tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's latest interest rate decision, expected Wednesday. Semiconductor stocks continued to face pressure amid concerns over AI capital spending and increasing competition from China. Oil prices extended their decline, offering some relief on inflation concerns.

items.headline: Shopify surged on strong software defensibility.
items.summary: Shopify jumped 11.54% following positive commentary from RBC highlighting its strong software defensibility using a new TCO model.

items.headline: Workday rose on AI-driven software commentary.
items.summary: Workday gained 9.0% today after RBC offered commentary on AI-driven software displacement and vendor defensibility, suggesting persistent strength.

items.headline: OPKO Health beat Q2 estimates and raised guidance.
items.summary: OPKO Health shares rose 9% after the company surpassed Q2 revenue and earnings estimates and subsequently raised its full-year revenue guidance.

items.headline: SanDisk dipped amid mixed AI chip headlines.
items.summary: SanDisk fell 11.02% due to recent target changes and mixed headlines surrounding memory and AI chips, continuing a multi-week decline.

items.headline: Venture Global declined on energy project news.
items.summary: Venture Global saw a 10.41% decline as traders reacted to headlines concerning its energy infrastructure projects.

items.headline: Lumentum Holdings dropped on president's departure.
items.summary: Lumentum Holdings dropped 6.69% following the announcement that its president will depart the company.

items.headline: Micron Technology slid in pre-market trading.
items.summary: Micron Technology slid 4.6% in pre-market trading, reflecting ongoing pressure on semiconductor stocks amid broader concerns in the AI chip sector.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Kicks Off Policy Meeting
items.summary: The Federal Reserve began its two-day policy meeting today, July 28, with a rate decision expected on Wednesday. Most economists anticipate the central bank will maintain its benchmark policy rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range, marking the fifth consecutive meeting without a change since December 2025. Attention will be on policymakers' guidance for future rate moves amidst mixed inflation signals.

items.headline: Big Tech Earnings and AI Spending Under Scrutiny
items.summary: A wave of major technology companies, including Amazon ($AMZN), Meta Platforms ($META), Apple ($AAPL), and Microsoft ($MSFT), are scheduled to report earnings this week. Investors are keenly watching for insights into corporate spending on artificial intelligence and its impact on the broader economy, especially after weakness in semiconductor stocks pressured the Nasdaq Composite on Monday.

items.headline: UPS Reports Strong Q2 Results, Raises Full-Year Guidance
items.summary: United Parcel Service ($UPS) announced second-quarter 2026 consolidated revenues of $22.8 billion and non-GAAP adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.76. The company also raised its guidance for consolidated revenue to approximately $91.2 billion for the full year 2026.

items.headline: Centene Corporation Increases 2026 EPS Guidance
items.summary: Centene Corporation ($CNC) reported second-quarter 2026 GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.19 and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $2.51. The company raised its 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to greater than $4.80, citing underlying business strength.

items.headline: JetBlue Exceeds Expectations, Sets 2028 EPS Target
items.summary: JetBlue Airways ($JBLU) announced second-quarter 2026 operating revenue of $2.7 billion, a 14.5% year-over-year increase, driven by strong demand. The airline introduced a long-term financial target of at least $1.00 in earnings per share for 2028.

items.headline: Oil Prices Continue to Decline on De-escalation Hopes
items.summary: Oil prices extended their decline on Tuesday, with Brent crude down 1.85% at $85.88 a barrel and WTI crude falling 1.31% to $81.20 a barrel. This follows significant drops on Monday, driven by a pause in hostilities between the U.S. and Iran, raising hopes for a broader de-escalation and easing inflation concerns.

items.headline: Semiconductor Sector Under Pressure, Consumer Staples Lead
items.summary: The semiconductor sector remained under pressure, with stocks like Micron Technology ($MU), AMD ($AMD), and Nvidia ($NVDA) experiencing declines due to escalating concerns over AI ecosystem financing and rising Chinese competition. Meanwhile, consumer staples and communication services were among the leading sectors at Monday's close.
